decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core pipeline business, Product A fits the firm's stated direction and existing capabilities, so management is likely to justify past investment and keep it unless results are clearly untenable.

Although it uses the firm's coating and metalworking skills, Product D is a more isolated and less central diversification move, making it the easiest product for management to abandon in favor of the established infrastructure business.

Product E is distant from the core offer but the firm publicly committed to it as a broader product line for municipal customers, so escalation of commitment makes management likely to continue and attribute weak traction to temporary conditions.

Product F is also outside the core range, yet its multiple-model line and adjacency to public-sector buyers support continued commitment, especially when managers can view disappointing sales as a temporary market issue rather than a strategic mistake.
